title: Iran Strikes Gulf Airports and Military Bases as Conflict Threatens Millions of Indians Across the Middle East
excerpt: Two US troops killed in Jordan as Iran retaliates against Gulf states hosting American forces, triggering airport closures and Level 3 travel advisories across the region where 8.5 million Indians live and work.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Iran launched strikes against US bases in Kuwait, Bahrain, and Jordan, escalating regional tensions.
  • Two US service members were killed in Jordan, marking the first fatalities since the ceasefire ended.
  • Kuwait suspended airport operations; EU advised airlines to avoid Gulf airspace amid rising threats.
  • Level 3 travel advisories issued for Gulf states, impacting 8.5 million Indians living and working there.
  • Iran launched missile and drone strikes against US military bases in Kuwait, Bahrain, and Jordan after a seventh consecutive night of American strikes on Iranian territory.
  • Two US service members were killed and one is missing in action following Iranian attacks on a base in Jordan on July 17.
  • Kuwait temporarily suspended airport operations; the EU aviation agency advised airlines to avoid airspace over the UAE, Bahrain, Kuwait, and Qatar.
  • The United States, Canada, and Australia issued Level 3 travel advisories for the Gulf region, where approximately 8.5 million Indians live and work.

Iran escalated its retaliatory campaign against US allies in the Gulf on Saturday, launching missile and drone barrages at military bases and infrastructure across Kuwait, Bahrain, and Jordan — killing two American service members and triggering airport closures that have thrown international air travel through the region into turmoil.

The strikes came after a seventh consecutive night of American attacks on Iranian military targets, marking the most dangerous week in the US-Iran conflict since a ceasefire collapsed on July 11. For the roughly 8.5 million Indians living across the Gulf states, the escalation has turned an already tense geopolitical situation into a direct threat to daily life and travel.

Deadly Attacks on US Forces

US Central Command confirmed on Saturday that two service members were killed in action on July 17 while defending against Iranian ballistic missile and drone attacks in Jordan. A third service member remains missing in action. Four additional troops were medically evacuated to hospitals in Jordan but have since been released.

The deaths mark the first US military fatalities since President Trump ended the ceasefire with Iran last week. CENTCOM did not disclose the specific location of the attack or the identities of the fallen troops, pending notification of their families.

"Since there is no international institution to prevent the savagery of the US military, we have no path before us except the Quranic command: 'Whoever attacks you, attack them in the same manner.'"

— Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps statement

Gulf Airports and Infrastructure Under Fire

Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said it struck a US military support centre at Camp Arifjan in Kuwait and destroyed a radar facility at Ali Al Salem Air Base. Kuwait temporarily suspended takeoff and landing operations at Kuwait International Airport after repeated missile and drone threats. A desalination plant and an oil facility operated by Kuwait Petroleum Corporation were also hit, causing significant damage and injuries.

In Bahrain, air defences were activated against incoming aerial threats at Sheikh Isa Air Base. The IRGC claimed it also destroyed at least two US fighter jets during an attack on the Al Azraq base in Jordan, though these claims could not be independently verified.

Travel Chaos for Indian Workers and Families

The European Union Aviation Safety Agency issued an advisory telling operators not to enter the airspace of Bahrain, Kuwait, Qatar, or the United Arab Emirates, including the affected section of the Gulf of Oman. Kuwait Airways was forced to reschedule most commercial services.

On July 17, the United States, Canada, and Australia simultaneously updated their Middle East travel advisories, classifying the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, Qatar, and Kuwait under Level 3 parameters — urging citizens to reconsider travel to or through these countries.

The disruption strikes at the heart of one of the world's most important aviation corridors. Airports in Dubai, Doha, Abu Dhabi, and Riyadh collectively handle millions of passengers monthly, serving as critical gateways linking Asia, Europe, Africa, and North America. Indian workers and families — who make up a significant portion of Gulf populations — face potential flight cancellations, diversions, and extended delays even on routes that do not originate in the region.

The Broader Conflict

Iran's Health Ministry reported that 50 people have been killed and more than 500 injured in US strikes over the past three weeks, according to the semi-official ILNA news agency. American strikes have targeted bridges, power facilities, port infrastructure, and military installations near the Strait of Hormuz and deeper inland in Sistan and Baluchistan Province.

Iran has resumed its blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, through which roughly 20 percent of the world's oil passes. Washington responded by blockading Iranian ports. Iran has also signalled it may push its Houthi allies in Yemen to close the Bab al-Mandeb strait at the mouth of the Red Sea, which would compound global shipping disruptions.

What to Watch

Indian embassies across the Gulf have not yet issued formal evacuation advisories, but community organizations in Kuwait and Bahrain have begun circulating emergency contact numbers and shelter information. The Indian government's response in the coming days will be closely watched — particularly whether it activates the kind of mass evacuation operations seen during previous Gulf crises, such as Operation Raahat during the 2015 Yemen conflict. For now, Indians in the region are advised to monitor embassy communications, avoid proximity to military installations, and maintain updated travel documents.
